why: rcl's `rcl_get_default_allocator()` (a macro over `rcutils_get_default_allocator`, which the extractor cannot see). Ours returns an allocator whose functions allocate nothing: every object lives in caller storage or the executor's carved backing (RFC-0105 D10). Platform constraint: no allocator. Inits that take one (`rclc_support_init`, `rclc_executor_init`, `rcl_clock_init`) accept NULL or this one and refuse any other, so a caller-supplied allocator is never silently ignored. phase-492 W1.b.
